question: The income of Raman is ₹34,000. He saves 28% of his income. If his income increases by 11% and expenditure increases by 30%, then his savings will:
solution:
**Given:**

Income of Raman = ₹34,000

Savings percentage = 28%

Income increase percentage = 11%

Expenditure increase percentage = 30%

**Formula Used:**

Savings = Income × Savings percentage

Expenditure = Income - Savings

New Income = Income × (1 + Income increase percentage / 100)

New Expenditure = Expenditure × (1 + Expenditure increase percentage / 100)

New Savings = New Income - New Expenditure

Change in Savings = New Savings - Old Savings

**Calculation:**

⇒ Old Savings = ₹34,000 × 28 / 100 = ₹9,520

⇒ Old Expenditure = ₹34,000 - ₹9,520 = ₹24,480

⇒ New Income = ₹34,000 × (1 + 11 / 100) = ₹34,000 × 1.11 = ₹37,740

⇒ New Expenditure = ₹24,480 × (1 + 30 / 100) = ₹24,480 × 1.30 = ₹31,824

⇒ New Savings = ₹37,740 - ₹31,824 = ₹5,916

⇒ Change in Savings = ₹5,916 - ₹9,520 = -₹3,604

**∴ The correct answer is decrease by ₹3,604.**
